title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Four warnings out of five were wrong
summary: The lifecycle pairing warning fired four times out of five for nothing on a real project. It sits in the Problems panel and is on by default, so every false one costs attention.

highlights.title: The back dispatcher is not a leak
highlights.description: A callback added to onBackPressedDispatcher needs no removal: the dispatcher belongs to the Activity and dies with it.

highlights.title: bind with no argument
highlights.description: The bind and unbind pair stands for the bindService family. A bind() with no argument binds nothing, and the warning named the receiver instead.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A callback added to onBackPressedDispatcher, directly or through requireActivity(), no longer asks for a release in onDestroy.
A bind() call with no argument is left alone. A bind with an argument is still tracked, and still clears once unbind appears in the mirror method.
Measured on a real project of 5088 sources: 132 files reach this check, and the warnings drop from 5 to 1.
